lead_with.title: From 10M exomes to answers
lead_with.text: Raw variants linked to EHRs are only the start. PhiTech's AI can **interpret variants in clinical context** and add pathway/network-level insight, making Truveta's genomic data more useful to pharma and health-system researchers.

lead_with.title: Ready for the multi-omics phase
lead_with.text: Truveta is storing samples for future multi-omics work. PhiTech already runs **multi-omics pipelines** (genomics + transcriptomics + epigenomics), so it can be the analytics partner when that phase starts.

company.text: Truveta (founded 2020, launched 2021 with 14 health systems, Seattle) is a **real-world intelligence** company built and owned by US health systems, now **30 members**. It combines de-identified EHR data (120M+ patients) with AI (Truveta Language Model) on Microsoft Azure and sells regulatory-grade evidence and insights to biopharma, researchers and public health. In **Jan 2025** it launched the **Truveta Genome Project** with **Regeneron** (sequencing at the Regeneron Genetics Center) and **Illumina**, aiming to sequence exomes from up to 10 million volunteers and link them to clinical records. 2026 news: **Johnathan Lancaster** named President & Chief Scientific Officer (Jan 26); a **real-time clinical trials** solution (Jan 27); a **clinical AI** collaboration with Knit Health (May 2026); CEO **Terry Myerson** stepping down with CTO **Jay Nanduri** and CMO **Ryan Ahern** as interim co-CEOs while the board searches (Sep 15).

financials.text: **Series C: $320M** (Jan 2025) from Regeneron ($119.5M), Illumina ($20M) and 17 health systems including Advocate Health, CommonSpirit and Northwell. No revenue published. Well funded, but in a **CEO transition**: new partnerships may need sign-off from the interim co-CEOs or Johnathan Lancaster.

industry.title: Genomics joins real-world data
industry.text: Linking sequencing to longitudinal health records (Truveta, All of Us, UK Biobank) is the new standard for target discovery and trial design.

industry.title: Multi-omics is the next layer
industry.text: DNA alone explains only part of disease. RNA and other omics on stored biospecimens are the next step, and they need specialised AI interpretation.

industry.title: Pharma buys insight, not raw data
industry.text: Real-world data vendors compete on analytics. Partners that turn genomic data into ready answers help win pharma contracts.

talking_points: Where is the **Truveta Genome Project** today: how many exomes are linked, and when will genomic data be in Truveta Studio?
Which **genomic analyses** do pharma customers ask for most, and which are hardest to deliver?

Does Truveta build interpretation tools in-house or **partner with specialist analytics companies**?
Would a **joint pilot on one cohort** be a good first step, and who else should join the next call?
